documents.title: Antora Environment :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Antora Environment Antora is our static website generator. We use it to generate the documentation of the project It is part of the documentation of Feel++ docs website. To generate the documentation $ npm install (1) $ npm run antora (2) $ npm run start (3) 1 Install the dependencies 2 Generate the documentation 3 Serve the documentation, the URL is provided in the console

documents.title: CMake Environment :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf CMake Environment The CMakeLists.txt is setup with Feel++. A sample Feel++ application is available in src. 1. Building The CMakeLists.txt is configured to build the application in src. The following commands can be used to build the application: $ cmake --preset default (1) $ cmake --build --preset default (2) $ cmake --build --preset default -t install (3) 1 Configure the project 2 Build the project 3 Install the project 2. Packaging CPack is configured and allows to generate a binary and source package. Use the following commands to generate the binary package: $ cmake --build --preset default -t package Use the following commands to generate the source package: $ cmake --build --preset default -t package_source 3. Testing CTest is configured. Use the following command to run the tests: $ cmake --build --preset default -t test

documents.title: GitHub Actions :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf GitHub Actions GitHub Actions are set up to build the documentation using Antora and upload them to docs.feelpp.org[Feel++ docs] upon any change in the repo. build, install, package and deliver the Feel++ code See the [workflow file](.github/workflows/ci.yml) for more details. 1. Skipping a job You can skip the CI by adding the following line in the commit message: [skip ci] You can skip the job that build the documentation by adding the following line in the commit message: doc skip. You can skip the job that build the code by adding the following line in the commit message: code skip.

documents.title: VS Code Integration :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf VS Code Integration The project is configured to integrate VSCode using Docker Container. The Docker image can be set from feelpp/feelpp or feelpp/feelpp-toolboxes, simply edit .devcontainer/Dockerfile and choose the image you want. ssh-keyscan is used on github.com to register the public key of github in $HOME/.ssh/known_hosts and avoid having git auth issues the first time we log into the container and push/pull to/from github. The following extensions are installed in Docker: cpptools cmaketools cmake asciidoctor-vscode

documents.title: Problem Set 1: RB for Linear Affine Elliptic Problems :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Problem Set 1: RB for Linear Affine Elliptic Problems We consider the problem of designing a thermal fin to effectively remove heat from a surface. The two-dimensional fin, shown in Figure 1, consists of a vertical central “post” and four horizontal “subfins”; the fin conducts heat from a prescribed uniform flux “source” at the root, \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{root}}\) , through the large-surface-area subfins to surrounding flowing air. The fin is characterized by a five-component parameter vector, or “input,” \(\mu_ = (\mu_1 , \mu_2, \ldots, \mu_5 )\),where \(\mu_i = k^i , i = 1, \ldots , 4\), and \(\mu_5 = \mathrm{Bi}\); \(\mu\) may take on any value in a specified design set \(D \subset \mathbb{R}^5\). Figure 1. Thermal fin Here \(k^i\) is the thermal conductivity of the ith subfin (normalized relative to the post conductivity \(k^0 \equiv 1\)); and \(\mathrm{Bi}\) is the Biot number, a nondimensional heat transfer coefficient reflecting convective transport t

Given the reduced basis approximation implemented in PS2, we turn to implementing the associated a posteriori error estimation procedures developed in the lecture. The second half of this problem set is devoted to implementing the greedy sampling procedure. documents.title: M2 ROM & Data-Driven ROM :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf M2 ROM & Data-Driven ROM How can a numerical model predict fast enough, assess its accuracy, and learn from measurements? This course develops methods useful for digital twins through lectures and hands-on notebook work. Master CSMI · Université de Strasbourg · Christophe Prud’homme 1. Start here Session 1 — Digital twins: models, observations and prediction Thursday 10 September 2026, 13:30–15:30 (Europe/Paris). Prepare your notebook environment and download the opening notebook. 2. A cours intégré We have 14 sessions of 2 hours, combining mathematical explanation, guided computation and discussion. You will construct reduced approximations, examine their errors and costs, and combine models with observations. Data assimilation is a required part of the course. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Practical Session on Implementing the Kalman Filter Method 1. Introduction The Kalman filter is a powerful mathematical tool used for estimating the state of a dynamic system from a series of noisy measurements. It is widely applied in areas like control systems, robotics, navigation, and finance. This session will guide you through implementing the Kalman filter with two simple examples: One-Dimensional Position Tracking Two-Dimensional Position and Velocity Estimation By the end of this session, you’ll understand how the Kalman filter works and how to implement it in practice. 2. Prerequisites Basic knowledge of linear algebra and probability theory Familiarity with programming in Python (or a similar language) Basic understanding of dynamic systems and state estimation 3. All files needed by students are published with the notebook; no mesh generator or private source collection is needed. These are nondimensional teaching experiments, not a calibrated industrial twin. For a prediction-first route, read the transient 2D thermal/POD overview: it explains time stepping, affine offline/online preparation and the trajectory error estimate before adding observations. Model and data The spatial operators describe conduction in five subregions and Robin heat loss on the exposed boundary. We set all five conductivities to one and vary the Biot number multiplying the boundary matrix. A supplied mass matrix enables a transient extension of the original spatial model: \[M\dot u+A(\mathrm{Bi})u=f g(t),\qquad A(\mathrm{Bi})=\sum_{q=0}^{4}A_q+\mathrm{Bi}\,A_5.\] The coarse grid has 1333 degrees of free

documents.title: Ensemble Kalman filtering and reduced forecasts :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Ensemble Kalman filtering and reduced forecasts Read the Kalman filter first. The EnKF propagates an ensemble through a possibly nonlinear model and estimates forecast covariances from its anomalies. It is not an exact nonlinear Bayesian filter; even an infinite ensemble need not make a non-Gaussian posterior Gaussian. Forecast and sample covariance Propagate each analysis member, adding independent process noise when that is part of the specified model. For \(N_e>1\) members, let \(X\) contain forecast states and \(Y\) their predicted observations. Subtract the respective ensemble means to obtain anomaly matrices. \[\begin{aligned} C_{xy}&=\frac{X'Y'^T}{N_e-1}, & C_{yy}&=\frac{Y'Y'^T}{N_e-1},\\ K&=C_{xy}(C_{yy}+R)^{-1}. \end{aligned}\] For linear observations, predicted observations are simply \(HX\). The anomaly matrix \(X'\in\mathbb R^{n\times N_e}\) has columns \(x_i-\bar x\) and satisfies \(X'\mathbf1=0\). Thus its rank, and the rank of its sample c

documents.title: GEIM: interpolation from sensor functionals :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf GEIM: interpolation from sensor functionals EIM observes point values. GEIM replaces those evaluations by bounded linear functionals from a sensor dictionary. Examples include localized averages, weighted integrals or linear observation operators. This is state reconstruction from measurements; fitting a conductivity parameter with nonlinear least squares is a different inverse problem. Declare the observation model Use a discrete state metric and measurement operator: \[\langle u,v\rangle_V=u^TGv,\qquad y=Hu+\varepsilon, \qquad G=G^T>0.\] For a sensor row \(h_s^T\), the measurement is \(\ell_s(v)=h_s^Tv\). The Riesz theorem identifies a state vector representing this functional: \[Gq_s=h_s,\qquad \ell_s(v)=q_s^TGv,\qquad \|\ell_s\|_{V_h'}=\sqrt{h_s^Tq_s}.\] A row of \(H\) contains the functional coefficients, not its Riesz representative. documents.title: Kalman filtering: forecasts and sequential observations :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Kalman filtering: forecasts and sequential observations Static reconstruction uses one observation vector. A filter propagates information through a dynamical model and updates it when new observations arrive. Time index and prior/posterior superscripts must remain distinct. Linear Gaussian model \[x_k=F_kx_{k-1}+b_k+w_k,\qquad y_k=H_kx_k+v_k, \qquad w_k\sim\mathcal N(0,Q_k),\quad v_k\sim\mathcal N(0,R_k).\] Assume the initial state is Gaussian, noises are temporally independent, and process, observation and initial errors are mutually independent. The covariances describe errors, not the temperature or other state’s absolute magnitude. Under these assumptions the Kalman filter computes the conditional mean and covariance exactly. With misspecified covariances its reported uncertainty need not be calibrated. Covariance: what uncertainty is propagated? documents.title: PBDW: background space and data-driven correction :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf PBDW: background space and data-driven correction Read observations and GEIM first. PBDW combines a low-dimensional background space with an update determined by measurements. The background is a space of plausible states; its coefficients are inferred from data, not supplied by the unknown true state. Riesz representatives and stability Each sensor is a bounded linear functional represented in the state inner product by a vector. Read the matrix derivation first: applying a sensor and taking the inner product with its representative must give the same value for every state. For state metric \(G\) and measurement matrix \(H\), solve \(GQ=H^T\) and define: \[Q=G^{-1}H^T,\quad W=\operatorname{range}(Q),\quad A=HQ=H G^{-1}H^T,\quad B=HZ.\] Columns of \(Z\) span the background. The identity between applying a functional and taking an inner product with its Riesz representative is: \[Hu=Q^TGu.\] For example, with \(G=hI\), point sensors have representatives s

documents.title: A computable lower bound for coercivity :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf A computable lower bound for coercivity The residual error bound divides the residual dual norm by a positive certified lower bound \(\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)\). This page constructs one such bound and states exactly when the inexpensive min-Theta formula is valid. What must be bounded? Fix a state norm \(\|\cdot\|_V\), independent of the parameter. For a coercive bilinear form, its best coercivity constant is \[\alpha(\mu)=\inf_{v\in V_h\setminus\{0\}} \frac{a_\mu(v,v)}{\|v\|_V^2}>0.\] We need a number that is guaranteed to satisfy \[0<\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)\leq\alpha(\mu) \qquad\text{for every admissible }\mu.\] For a discrete matrix \(A(\mu)\) and fixed positive-definite Gram matrix \(G\), this is the smallest generalized eigenvalue of the symmetric part \(A_s(\mu)=(A(\mu)+A(\mu)^T)/2\) relative to \(G\): \[\alpha(\mu)=\min_{\mathbf v\ne0} \frac{\mathbf v^TA_s(\mu)\mathbf v}{\mathbf v^TG\mathbf v}.\] Solving this full-dimensional eigenproblem at e

Three changes, three questions Extension What changes? What remains useful? documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf A posteriori error estimation for coercive reduced models The practical question is whether a cheap reduced prediction is accurate enough at a new parameter, without solving the full model again. A residual becomes a bound only after combining it with stability information in consistent norms. Here \(\alpha(\mu)=\inf_{v\ne0}a_\mu(v,v)/\|v\|_V^2\) is the coercivity constant and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)\) is a verified positive lower bound satisfying \(0<\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)\leq\alpha(\mu)\). The coercivity lower-bound page derives a cheap min-Theta choice from a positive affine decomposition and explains its assumptions. Prerequisites: Galerkin reduction and Hilbert spaces, dual norms and Riesz representation. Core course route: understand the residual functional, compute its norm with a Riesz solve, derive the bound and interpret effectivity. The final offline residual factorization is optional advanced reading; it is not required for the session

documents.title: Digital twins: connecting models and observations :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Digital twins: connecting models and observations A useful numerical model answers a question about a physical system. A digital-twin setting adds observations of that system and a process for updating the digital representation as the system evolves. Begin with a purpose Consider a heated component monitored by a few temperature sensors. We want to estimate its temperature field, predict a quantity such as a peak temperature, and decide whether a proposed operating condition is acceptable. The sensors observe only part of the state; the model supplies information between sensors and supports predictions under changed conditions. For this material, a digital twin is a digital representation associated with a physical system, informed by observations and used for a defined purpose such as monitoring, prediction or decision support. The required update frequency follows that purpose: a temperature-monitoring task and a long-term maintenance study need diff

documents.title: Hilbert spaces, dual norms and Riesz representation :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Hilbert spaces, dual norms and Riesz representation A residual or a sensor is a rule acting on a state. A state norm measures vectors; a dual norm measures these rules. This page explains the connection needed to compute residual bounds and to construct data-assimilation updates. Course route: read through the matrix example before session 3. The function-space example and the existence proof are supplementary reading. The efficient offline/online implementation of a certificate is separate advanced reading. From inner products to linear functionals A real inner-product space has a symmetric bilinear product \((u,v)_V\) that is positive on every nonzero vector. It defines the norm \(\|v\|_V=\sqrt{(v,v)_V}\). A Hilbert space is complete in this norm: every Cauchy sequence converges to an element of the space. Finite-dimensional spaces with positive definite inner products are Hilbert spaces. Completeness matters for infinite-dimensional spaces of function

documents.title: DEIM: POD-based empirical interpolation :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf DEIM: POD-based empirical interpolation Read non-affinity and EIM first. DEIM constructs a POD basis of source or nonlinear-term snapshots, then chooses interpolation coordinates for that basis. The state basis and nonlinear-term basis have different roles and generally different dimensions. Construction Let the columns of \(U_m\) be Euclidean-orthonormal POD modes of the term to approximate. Choose the largest-magnitude entry of the first mode. For each subsequent mode, interpolate it using previous modes and points, then choose the largest-magnitude residual entry. The new point cannot repeat an earlier one while the residual is nonzero. \[D_m f=U_m(P_m^TU_m)^{-1}P_m^Tf.\] Use a linear solve; the inverse in the formula is not an instruction to compute an explicit inverse in code. Interpolation is exact at the selected coordinates and on the span of the retained modes. Euclidean error bound For orthonormal \(U_m\), distinct selected coordinates and nons

documents.title: Non-affinity and empirical interpolation :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Non-affinity and empirical interpolation An affine decomposition separates parameter dependence from spatial operators: \[A(\mu)=\sum_{q=1}^{Q_a}\theta_q(\mu)A_q, \qquad f(\mu)=\sum_{q=1}^{Q_f}\eta_q(\mu)f_q.\] The worked affine prediction example shows exactly which arrays are stored and used at a query. For small fixed numbers of terms, projected matrices and vectors are assembled offline. A moving Gaussian source or a nonlinear constitutive law generally lacks such a small exact decomposition. Evaluating the entire source or nonlinear residual online can then dominate the reduced solve. Empirical interpolation constructs a separable approximation whose coefficients are determined from selected evaluations. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Reduced bases and Galerkin prediction How can repeated predictions become cheaper while retaining the structure of the governing equations? We first assume a linear, coercive problem and a fixed reduced trial space. See notation for state vectors, norms and observations. Course route: understand the solution family, snapshot construction, Galerkin equations, stability and affine prediction. The compliant-output result explains an important special case in the error analysis. Supplementary remarks extend the interpretation without adding a new required practical. Why a reduced basis can represent a large model The input is a parameter vector: material coefficients, boundary data, forcing amplitudes or geometry can vary. The desired result may be a temperature average, a displacement or a sensor prediction, rather than every degree of freedom. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Greedy reduced bases and POD Read POD and residual certificates first. POD minimizes an average squared projection error for a declared snapshot distribution and state metric. A reduced-basis greedy algorithm instead seeks a space that controls the largest estimated reduced-solve error on a finite training set. Neither criterion alone guarantees accuracy outside that set. Certified selection Let the discrete model be coercive, with reduced space \(V_r\) and a computable certificate: \[\|u_h(\mu)-u_r(\mu)\|_V\leq\Delta_r(\mu) =\frac{\|f_\mu-a_\mu(u_r,\cdot)\|_{V_h'}}{\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)}.\] Here the numerator is a dual norm on the full discrete test space, not the norm of the reduced-system residual. For the candidate prediction, form \(\rho=f-AZa\), solve \(Gz_R=\rho\), and use \[\Delta_r(\mu)=\frac{\sqrt{\rho^Tz_R}}{\alpha_{\mathrm{LB}}(\mu)}.\] The Riesz representation notes explain why this solve computes the supremum in the dual norm.
